articles.title: Daniel Roseberry adds ‘aerodynamic‘ edge to Schiaparelli’s surrealist glamour at Paris show
articles.summary: American in Paris showcases new simplicity with stretch cocktail frocks, but there’s still plenty of gold-foiled nipples and peekaboo fabrics to wow the frow. In a world of mega brands, the house of Schiaparelli is small but perfectly formed.
body: However, the Schiaparelli name punches above its weight. An exhibition at London’s V&A museum this year made a strong case for its founder, Elsa Schiaparelli, who collaborated with Salvador Dali and Jean Cocteau, as a creative force in the surrealism movement of the 1930s.

Kylie Jenner in a dress adorned with a fake lion’s head and Bella Hadid on the Cannes red carpet with an elaborate gold necklace covering her breasts have put the brand name all over TikTok. “It’s an amazing time at Schiap,” designer Daniel Roseberry said after his Paris show. “It’s a smaller house, but I feel like the voice is so big. It’s exclusive, but it’s real, because what we show on the catwalk is exactly what we sell.”

Schiap – Elsa’s nickname has become a nickname for her house – is strong meat. In his haute couture collections, Roseberry has leaned into Schiaparelli’s visual signature of anatomical detail parlayed into glamour. A tight dress might have a padded spine, gloves embroidered with glossy red fingernails, a jacket buttoned with a row of tiny gold ears or noses.
points: American in Paris showcases new simplicity with stretch cocktail frocks, but there’s still plenty of gold-foiled nipples and peekaboo fabrics to wow the frow.

articles.title: They’re delicious, popular and versatile – but how healthy are berries?
articles.summary: Experts say that if you’re eating any berry – strawberries, blackberries, currants, raspberries, blueberries – you are benefiting. Sprinkled on top of yoghurt, blended into smoothies or baked into crumbles, berries are among Americans’ favorite fruits.
body: Luckily, berries are as healthy as they are delicious and versatile: low in calories, full of vitamins and antioxidants, and a good source of fiber. Research shows that, depending on the type, berries support cardiovascular health, may boost gut health and fight inflammation and show promise as part of a “healthy dietary strategy for diabetes prevention and management”, to quote researchers. Meta-analyses also link compounds in berries with improved cognitive health.
“Berries’ high polyphenol content is what we think makes them so protective” when it comes to mental processes such as memory and attention, said Maggie Moon, a registered dietitian.

Polyphenols are a broad category of plant compounds; in berries, the most active and proportionally meaningful of them are anthocyanins, which also give many berries their blue, purple and red pigments.

Researchers are investigating whether berry polyphenols and the metabolites produced when gut microbes process them may influence inflammation and blood-vessel function. Because the brain depends on an extensive blood supply, better vascular function is one plausible route by which berries could support cognition.
points: Experts say that if you’re eating any berry – strawberries, blackberries, currants, raspberries, blueberries – you are benefiting.
Sprinkled on top of yoghurt, blended into smoothies or baked into crumbles, berries are among Americans’ favorite fruits.

articles.title: This Wedding Weekend at an Irish Manor Featured Bespoke Looks, Plenty of Vintage, and a Pajama Party
articles.summary: Noah Zgralich and Lauren Huff held an Adare Manor wedding weekend filled with golf and pub crawls. The bride wore looks from House of Gilles, Ralph Lauren, Elie Saab, and Alexander McQueen throughout the celebration.
body: Lauren Huff and Noah Zgrablich pretended to be newlyweds on the very first day they met. In 2017, the two were both guests at their mutual friend’s black-tie 21st birthday party in New York City. “Lauren was wearing a long white dress that I still remember brought out the blue in her eyes,” recalls Noah. They went with their friends to another bar after the party and, as a joke, Noah told other patrons around that they just come from their wedding. “They kept buying us free drinks, which definitely made her laugh,” he says. “We even have a photo together from that night.”

It would take four more years before their real relationship would begin. Lauren was visiting a friend in Los Angeles and mentioned on Instagram that they were off to O’Brien’s Irish Pub and Restaurant. Noah convinced his friends to go and messaged her back, “What a coincidence, we’re actually on our way there.” After spending time together, he convinced Lauren to go on a date with him before she flew back home.

articles.title: Brimful of personality: the rise of fashion’s ‘silly little hats’
articles.summary: From pillboxes and boaters to bicornes and buckets, characterful hats are making their way from the catwalk to the high street. “Here goes – an order for a million hats,” wrote Jackie Kennedy to Bergdorf Goodman before moving into the White House in the early 1960s.
body: This season at the turbo-high-end brand Loro Piana, whose clothes are beloved by tech bros and Kendall Roy, almost every model was wearing a hat. At Thom Browne, straw boaters came shrouded in colourful mesh. At Chloé there were see-through hats to match see-through trenchcoats and white sailor hats atop all-white outfits. Courrège’s hats were space-age, Burberry had big buckets, Bottega Veneta had hats brimming with charisma.

Some are calling them “personality hats”, others, affectionately, “silly little hats”, but hats that foreground character over practicality are enjoying time spent on heads from Milan fashion week to the shops. It’s not about a sou’wester in a storm but a creative punctuation point to an outfit, meant to draw the eye upwards.

Hats are a great expression of personality. According to David Long, the author of The Hats That Made Britain: A History of the Nation Through Its Headwear: “Excluding beanies and baseballs, hats are a rare opportunity for display, so I think the wearers are trying to say: ‘I’m not like everyone else, even though we all wear the same clothes nowadays.’ They’re showing off, in other words, but only a little bit.”

articles.title: Shaun Tan: ‘We’re always only seeing a thin skin of reality’
articles.summary: One of Australia’s most cherished and awarded picture book illustrators on what makes a good painting, the mechanics of life and the fine line between utopia and dystopia.
body: “In my day-to-day life, I’m not creative at all,” Tan says as we prepare to take his strange and wondrous creature – AKA French bulldog Reuben – for a walk in the local Brunswick West dog park near where Tan lives with his artist wife Inari. “But when I sit down to draw, it’s like a moment to pause and question: what does all this mean? And how come I live like this and not another way?”

“I have this theory that if a painting is really good a five-year-old can still get something out of it,” Tan says. “A good painting should hit you in an emotional way.” Often he will haul one of his kids into the studio to see their reaction to a piece he’s working on. “A bit happy and a bit creepy? Great, that’s what I wanted. You can go now.”

What he had was enthusiasm, an interest that would become keener with time, and parents who were warmly encouraging. “They just said: you seem to love doing this.” They found a specialist art high school in the suburb of Balcatta for him, where he developed his unique craft. “I learned most of my basic artistic skills that I use today in high school. I don’t think I’ve had any formal illustration training since then.”

articles.title: Is Getting Back With an Ex Ever a Good Idea?
articles.summary: Don’t do it because you’re lonely, or because dating has become exhausting—and certainly not because your time on the apps has convinced you humanity is doomed.
body: I’ve always believed that timing is everything. Sometimes life pulls us away from the people or things that are meant for us, and we have no choice but to let go and make room for whatever comes next. Other times, if we’re lucky, life has a funny way of bringing us back to what we thought we’d lost.

In March 2023, when COVID finally began loosening its grip and the world came alive again, I found myself at an art fundraiser in Midtown Manhattan, dressed in Chanel and sipping a martini in a room of mostly strangers. The restaurant was loud, with photographers circling the art patrons like vultures. Then I spotted my ex next to the seafood bar.

There are few things more destabilizing than seeing an ex in the wild. Thankfully, I wasn’t in sweats running around the East Village. (Timing, as I said, is everything.) He looked up, we locked eyes, and my stomach dropped immediately.

This is the problem with exes. When you meet someone new, the uncertainty is exciting. You wonder if they like you. You wonder if they’re attracted to you. You wonder if they’ll call. It’s all very thrilling and hypothetical.

articles.title: Where Was Youth Filmed: Sharon Horgan’s Latest Divorce Comedy Comes to London
articles.summary: The new HBO series starring the likes of Rupert Friend and Sharlene Whyte features some cool London locations—plus one much-loved overseas stop.
body: On Location peels back the curtain on some of your favourite films, television shows, and more. This time, we ask: where was Youth filmed?

Sharon Horgan is behind so many TV shows that we know and love, including the darkly funny Bad Sisters, Pulling, Catastrophe, and hilarious Motherland. Shows that will forever remain iconic to audiences around the world. And now, she’s back with her latest project, Youth. The new eight-episode HBO series follows a 50-year-old divorcée (played by Horgan herself) who finds herself single again and searching for love and intimacy, while navigating her career, caring for her elderly parents, and her troubled 18-year-old son (played by Cillian Murphy’s son, Aran).

As well as love and divorce, Youth also examines the online influences shaping teenage boys through the character of Alex’s son Ruari, who is struggling emotionally and being fed distorted ideas of masculinity in the digital sphere.

The series stars Rupert Friend, Sharlene Whyte, Aran Murphy, and Robbie Gee, with Harriet Walter, Anne Reid, Freddie Fox, and Damian Lewis also appearing in supporting and guest roles throughout the show.

articles.summary: Following Thursday evening’s vernissage for Rafael Pavarotti: Photographer at the Musée des Arts Décoratifs, dinner guests including Katie Holmes, Lauryn Hill, and Karlie Kloss made their way to Solum Paris, where the mise-en-scène seemed lifted from one of Pavarotti's color-saturated images…
body: Under the artistic direction of Igi Lola Ayedun, with production by La Mode en Images, the space became a study in scarlet for the evening. Every decorative element followed the same monochromatic register, from cantilever chairs and table linens to lush floral arrangements by Stéphane Chapelle, filled with Spartacus and Chat Noir dahlias, castor bean flowers, heliconia, ornamental pineapple, protea, nutans, grapes, and peppers. Red lighting further heightened the effect.

The soirée, presented in partnership with Brazilian luxury group Iguatemi, celebrated the Vogue contributor’s first major museum exhibition, a career milestone he has achieved at just 33 years old. Open to the public from today, Rafael Pavarotti: Photographer is curated by Sébastien Quéquet, curator in charge of the museum’s photographic collections, with scenography by longtime collaborator, Ibby Njoya.

articles.title: One Vogue Writer Puts L’Oréal’s Viral Moisturizer to the Test
articles.summary: Can you find a drugstore moisturizer that gives pricier picks a run for their money? In short, yes! One Vogue writer tests L’Oréal’s Revitalift Triple Power moisturizer.
body: Despite its oh-so-French name, L’Oréal is one of those tried-and-true brands you can find on most pharmacy shelves—and it’s not unusual to see a product in a friend’s, mother’s, or auntie’s bathroom cabinet. But with more skin-care options than ever—from niche and luxury brands to medical-grade formulas—do drugstore staples still hold up? And can they deliver the same results as their pricier counterparts?

Take, for example, L’Oréal’s Revitalift line, including its best-selling moisturizer. Sure, $30 is definitely a bit more spendy than your average drugstore moisturizer, but given its trio of active ingredients—hydronic acid, retinol, and vitamin C—it’s definitely more affordable than its luxury counterparts with similar formulations. Scroll on to discover one writer’s experience testing the bestselling product.

articles.title: The Top 10 Countries for Retiring Abroad, According to the 2026 Global Retirement Index
articles.summary: From sunny European climes to South American surf hubs, these are the best countries for globe-trotting retirees.
body: There is a point in life when everyone inevitably starts dreaming of retirement. For me, these thoughts came unexpectedly when I was just about to enter my 30s. Retirement seemed like a very far-away concern, but also one that required a bit of thought considering the difficulties that millennials and Gen Z are now facing—namely, the rising cost of living, a dire housing market, and a retirement age that is only getting higher.

There are quite a few aspects to consider when deciding where to retire. For me, quality of life, mild weather, and a good healthcare system are high priorities, as well as having a pre-existing network of friends and family. For others, dual citizenship options, tax optimization, and cost of living may be of more importance.

This is where the 2026 Global Retirement Report and Index comes in, a new report compiled by Global Citizen Solutions. The annual index compares 46 residency programs across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Africa. Importantly, every country on the list has a residency route aimed at retirees or financially independent people, such as Portugal's D7 Visa and Spain's Non-Lucrative Visa.
points: From sunny European climes to South American surf hubs, these are the best countries for globe-trotting retirees.

articles.title: The Unwritten Rules of Visiting Las Vegas
articles.summary: What happens here doesn't (necessarily) stay here, and there are a few things you'll want to do right.
body: Las Vegas can be a disorienting place to visit. Over 85,000 hotel rooms crammed into a single corridor. A reputation for nickel-and-diming. Extreme heat. And far too many escalators.

But the city’s unique mythology—bright lights and round-the-clock entertainment for 55-year-olds and 5-year-olds alike—keeps people coming back. And despite the city’s incessant need to modernize and reinvent itself, it remains the larger-than-life, slightly flamboyant entertainment capital it was back in the 1950s, when crowds first took notice of the strange casino town in the middle of the desert.
“Old movies like Casino gave Vegas cachet,” says Juyoung Kang, who has helmed mixology programs on and off the Strip since the early 2000s. “You don’t find that character anywhere else.”

Kang, who currently oversees the bar program at Doberman Drawing Room, has lived and worked in Vegas for years. But she says she never fell out of love with what makes Vegas classic. “I’ve been to Caesars Palace so many times,” she says, “and somehow I still get excited seeing all the statues and the fountains."

articles.title: Gabon's Isolated Wilderness and Rich Culture Make It a Safari Destination Beyond Compare
articles.summary: The central African nation is a precious discovery for those who appreciate what it means to be wild.
body: Furious chanting followed by a sharp inhalation of breath announced Marumba’s arrival. Swaddled in thick ruffles of raffia topped with a crown of feathers and a wooden mask in red, white, and black, the garish character crawled into view across a corrugated iron roof. Running at me, I would later learn, was the spirit’s perverse form of benediction. Dancers brandishing palm leaves backflipped and cartwheeled, pushing the mobile haystack into various corners until he gave one final frenzied shimmy and disappeared in a cloud of ash and smoke.

The ritual I’d witnessed belongs to Bwiti, a spiritual discipline rooted in Gabon’s dense, impenetrable forests. A commune on the edge of capital city of Libreville, Mikumu offers an education center, traditional healing clinic, and social services for young people. At its core is a determination to preserve a precious connection between culture and the natural world.
points: The central African nation is a precious discovery for those who appreciate what it means to be wild.
